# Locality Guide: Berkshire County, Massachusetts (1820–1850)

## Jurisdiction Overview

Berkshire County, Massachusetts was established in 1761, bordered by New York to the west and Vermont to the north — making it a genuinely cross-jurisdictional research challenge. The county is in the continuous western hill country and fell under Massachusetts general law throughout this period.

---

## Important Correction to the Research Premise

The assumption that "nothing civil exists before 1841" needs adjustment. The FamilySearch Wiki's *Massachusetts Vital Records* page (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Massachusetts_Vital_Records) confirms that **town-level recording of births, marriages, and deaths was ordered as early as 1639** in Massachusetts. While not all towns complied fully, this town-level civil system continued without interruption through the 1820–1850 period. What began in **1841** was a *statewide, centralized* recording system layered on top of the pre-existing town series. The 1841 act did not create the first civil records — it created the first *state-level* ones.

A digitized Berkshire County volume has been confirmed: **imageGroupNumber 004500891**, "Town Clerk Vital and Town Records," covering 1761–1850 (512 images). It is **browse-only** — 0% indexed, not name-searchable — but it exists and covers this period. Church and cemetery records remain essential, but they supplement rather than replace the town books.

---

## Record Types and Availability

### 1. Town Vital Records (Civil)

| Detail | Notes |
|---|---|
| **Period covered** | Town-level: from the 1600s onward; statewide centralized: 1841 (Boston excluded until 1850) |
| **FamilySearch collection** | "Massachusetts, Town Vital Records, 1620–1890" (collection id 2061550, ~3.4 million people) |
| **Berkshire-specific volume** | imageGroupNumber **004500891** — Town Clerk Vital and Town Records, 1761–1850, 512 images, **browse-only** |
| **Marriage note** | Marriage intentions were "commonly recorded in the bride's home town," with additional recordings in the groom's town and current residence — search **all three** locations |
| **Gaps** | No name index; must be browsed page by page; compliance varies by town |

### 2. Church Records

| Detail | Notes |
|---|---|
| **Confirmed denomination** | Congregational, Pittsfield, Berkshire County |
| **FamilySearch volume** | imageGroupNumber **004500892** — "Church Records (Congregational)," Pittsfield, 1791–1850, 274 images, **browse-only** (0% indexed) |
| **Statewide collection** | "Massachusetts, Church Records, 1630–1920" (collection id 1921657, ~987,000 people) |
| **Gaps** | No other denomination for Berkshire County was returned by the survey tools; border-town congregations (near New York or Vermont) were not confirmed — these should be investigated separately |
| **Language** | English |

### 3. Cemetery Records

| Detail | Notes |
|---|---|
| **Status** | No specific Berkshire cemeteries were returned by survey tools |
| **Online resource** | **Find A Grave** (https://www.findagrave.com/) is confirmed as a curated external resource for Massachusetts; county-specific coverage not detailed |
| **Importance** | Before 1841 (and wherever towns underrecorded), cemetery inscriptions are a **primary source**, not a backup — treat them as such |
| **Physical records** | Sexton/burial registers for individual towns are likely held locally; not confirmed online by this survey |

### 4. Federal Census Records

| Year | Coverage |
|---|---|
| 1820, 1830, 1840 | Names heads of household only; lists other members by age/sex groupings |
| 1850 | First census to name every individual — a major breakthrough for this period |

No Berkshire-specific census collection was returned by `collections_search`; access through FamilySearch or Ancestry general U.S. census collections.

### 5. Probate Records

**"Massachusetts, Probate Records, 1635–1991"** (FamilySearch collection id 1678901, ~567,000 people) spans the full period. Probate documents (wills, administrations, inventories, guardianships) often supply birth/death dates and family relationships that vital records miss.

### 6. Immigration and Naturalization

- **"Massachusetts, Passenger Lists, 1820–1891"** (collection id 1784312) — Berkshire is inland, so this applies mainly to family members arriving through Boston or New York ports.
- **"Massachusetts, Naturalization Records, 1790–1906"** (collection id 1459213) — naturalizations could be generated by any court, including those in Berkshire County.

---

## Repository Guide

### Online
| Repository | What it holds for this place |
|---|---|
| **FamilySearch** | Town vital records (collection 2061550); church records (collection 1921657); probate records (collection 1678901); digitized browse-only Berkshire volumes (004500891 and 004500892); passenger lists; naturalization records |
| **Find A Grave** | Cemetery inscriptions (https://www.findagrave.com/) |
| **Newspapers.com** | Obituaries and marriage notices as pre-registration substitutes (https://www.newspapers.com/) |
| **Ancestry.com** | U.S. Federal Census, 1820–1850 |
| **Fold3** | Military records, supplementary (https://www.fold3.com/) |

### Physical
| Repository | Holdings |
|---|---|
| **Town clerks of Berkshire County towns** | Original town vital records (originals stay with the town/city clerk, per the Massachusetts Vital Records Wiki page) |
| **Pittsfield Congregational church** | Original register underlying FamilySearch volume 004500892 |

> **Note:** `catalog_search` returned **zero hits** for Berkshire, Massachusetts — a cataloguing gap in the FamilySearch Catalog at the county level. Search again by individual town name, as town-specific microfilm may be catalogued separately.

---

## Known Record Losses

No record destruction or loss for Berkshire County during this period was returned by any tool in this survey. Gaps in indexing above reflect digitization coverage, not necessarily missing original records.

---

## Cross-Border Research (Critical for This Family)

Because the family's town sits close to **both the New York and Vermont lines**, the same vital, church, and cemetery searches must be repeated in the adjoining New York and Vermont jurisdictions. Members of a border-town family routinely crossed county and state lines for marriages, church membership, and burial. The specific adjoining counties could not be named from tool results in this survey and should be identified by locating the town on a period map.

---

## Research Tips

1. **Don't skip the town books.** The 1820–1850 period has town-level civil records even before 1841 — browse imageGroupNumber 004500891 page by page for the relevant towns.
2. **Search three places for every marriage** — the bride's town, the groom's town, and their place of residence, all of which may hold separate marriage-intention entries.
3. **The two confirmed Berkshire volumes are browse-only.** Budget time for manual image review; name-based searching will not work for either.
4. **Cemetery inscriptions are primary sources here**, not supplements — treat a gravestone as equivalent in standing to a town book entry for the pre-1841 years.
5. **Extend every search across the state lines.** New York and Vermont church registers, cemeteries, and vital records may hold the only surviving documentation of events this border family experienced.
6. **Check the FamilySearch Catalog by town name**, not county, since the county-level catalog search returned nothing — microfilm for individual Berkshire towns may be catalogued under the town.
7. **Consult the FamilySearch Wiki pages** for `Massachusetts_Church_Records`, `Berkshire_Massachusetts_Genealogy`, and your specific town — those pages were not retrieved in this survey and may supply denomination-specific and town-specific detail beyond what is confirmed here.

## Locality Guide: Billy Civil Parish, County Antrim, Ireland (c. 1780–1870)

### Jurisdiction Overview

**Billy civil parish** lies partly in the barony of Carey and chiefly in the barony of Lower Dunluce, within the poor law union of Coleraine, County Antrim, Ulster. Its principal town is **Bushmills**. The parish also contains part of Dunserverick.

**Ecclesiastical background:** Billy was formerly the head of an ecclesiastical union comprising Armoy, Ballyclug, Donegore, and Kilbride — worth knowing if any pre-1825 family event was recorded under one of those parishes rather than Billy itself.

**Religious makeup confirmed by the FamilySearch Wiki:**
The parish had meeting houses for **Presbyterians**, for **Covenanters** (Reformed Presbyterians — a stricter, separate tradition), and for **Wesleyan Methodists**, alongside the **Church of Ireland** parish church. Roman Catholic families fell within the district of Coleraine. This is the most important jurisdictional fact for your research: "Presbyterian" in Billy parish could mean two distinct congregations (mainstream Presbyterian and the separate Covenanter meeting house), each keeping its own register.

---

### Record Types Available

#### Church Records — Primary Source for 1780–1870

This is the core source for a Presbyterian family before civil registration begins. The FamilySearch Wiki's Billy Civil Parish page has distinct sections for each denomination (Catholic, Church of Ireland, Presbyterian, Methodist, Society of Friends, Others), but the fill-in detail — register start dates, repository, film numbers — did not render from the tools in this survey for Billy specifically.

**What the nearby Ballylinny Civil Parish page (County Antrim) shows as the standard pattern:** Presbyterian baptism and marriage registers starting in 1837, originals with the local church, microfilm at PRONI (film MIC 1P/327, from 1851) and the FamilySearch Library (film 973220, from 1837). **Do not apply Ballylinny's dates or film numbers to Billy** — this is cited only to show what information to look for when you pull Billy's own page.

**Action needed:** Fetch the Billy Civil Parish wiki page's Presbyterian subsection directly on FamilySearch's website, or consult PRONI's register guide for Billy/Bushmills-area Presbyterian congregations by name. Confirm which congregation your family attended *first*, since there were at least two distinct Presbyterian traditions locally.

#### Civil Registration of Vital Records

Irish civil registration has distinct start dates for different events (non-Catholic marriages registered earlier than general birth/death registration). These dates are well known but were not confirmed by a retrieved page in this session, so verify them directly on the FamilySearch Wiki's Ireland Civil Registration page. The relevant modern repository for Northern Ireland is **GRONI** (General Register Office of Northern Ireland).

#### Census Records

The original Irish census returns for 1821–1851 were largely destroyed (1861 and 1871 returns were also lost); this is general knowledge not confirmed by a retrieved page in this survey. **Standard substitutes:**
- **Tithe Applotment Books** (1820s–30s): survey of landholders for tithe purposes — a valuable pre-census substitute
- **Griffith's Valuation** (mid-19th century): comprehensive survey of property occupiers

Coverage of Billy parish by these sources was not confirmed by tool results in this session — verify at PRONI or on findmypast.ie/Ancestry.

#### Probate Records

Before 1858, Irish probate went through diocesan/consistorial courts; for Antrim, that falls within the Diocese of Connor. After 1858, district probate registries. This is general knowledge, not confirmed by a retrieved source in this session — verify independently.

#### Land Records

The Tithe Applotment Books and Griffith's Valuation (noted above) are the primary pre-1870 land/occupier substitutes for Ireland.

---

### Repositories

| Repository | Role | Access |
|---|---|---|
| **PRONI** (Public Record Office of Northern Ireland) | Standard holder of Presbyterian and other Ulster church register microfilm; also holds Tithe Books, Griffith's, estate papers | In-person Belfast; online catalogue at nidirect.gov.uk/proni |
| **GRONI** (General Register Office of Northern Ireland) | Civil registration of births, marriages, deaths | groni.gov.uk |
| **FamilySearch Library** | Microfilm copies of many PRONI-held registers | FamilySearch.org catalog; some digitized online |
| **FamilySearch Wiki — Billy Civil Parish page** | Framework for which denominations had registers; links to film numbers once subsections load | familysearch.org/en/wiki/Billy_Civil_Parish |

---

### Key Research Tips

1. **Two Presbyterian congregations, two registers.** The parish had a mainstream Presbyterian meeting house *and* a separate Covenanter (Reformed Presbyterian) meeting house. Identify which one your family attended before ordering a register — wrong congregation means wrong record set.

2. **The ecclesiastical union may hold earlier entries.** Billy was head of a union with Armoy, Ballyclug, Donegore, and Kilbride. If the Billy register starts after 1825 or is thin for the 1780s–1820s, check whether earlier entries appear under one of those associated parishes.

3. **Pull the Billy wiki page directly.** The FamilySearch Wiki page for Billy civil parish has the denomination-by-denomination church records section with register dates and film numbers — but that detail did not render from the tools in this survey. Go to [Billy Civil Parish, County Antrim, Northern Ireland Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Billy_Civil_Parish,_County_Antrim,_Northern_Ireland_Genealogy#Church_records) and look at the Presbyterian subsection for exact dates and PRONI/FHL film references.

4. **Tool coverage gap — not a records gap.** Several lookup tools (place lookup, collections search, catalog search) could not resolve County Antrim / Northern Ireland in this session. Treat every absence in this guide as a gap in what the tools returned, not as confirmation that records are undigitized or missing. PRONI and the FamilySearch catalog will have more than what this survey could surface.

output.text_response:
# Locality Guide: County Cork, Ireland (1830s–1840s)

## Jurisdiction Overview
County Cork, located in Munster province, was under British administration in this period. Cork City served as the county seat. The population was predominantly Roman Catholic with a Church of Ireland (Anglican) minority — a critical distinction since it determines which church kept your ancestor's records.

**Key historical events affecting records:**
- The Great Famine began 1845, just at the end of this target window, driving mass emigration
- The **1922 Four Courts fire** in Dublin destroyed most pre-1901 census returns, wills, and many government records — a defining limitation for Irish research

---

## Available Record Types

### Vital Records (Civil Registration)
⚠️ **No civil certificates exist for the 1830s–1840s.** Civil registration of births, deaths, and Roman Catholic marriages did not begin until **1 January 1864**. Non-Catholic marriages were registered from 1845 — but that's the very end of your window, and only for a minority. **Church registers are your only substitute.**

---

### Church Records *(primary vital-event source)*
- **Roman Catholic registers:** Baptisms and marriages (rarely burials). Many Cork parishes' registers begin in the 1810s–1830s, so coverage for your period is plausible — but survival varies parish by parish.
  - **Held online:** The **National Library of Ireland** (www.registers.nli.ie) offers free digital images of Catholic parish registers up to 1880.
- **Church of Ireland (Anglican) registers:** Held by the **Representative Church Body Library** and in local parish custody.
- **Critical first step:** You must identify your ancestor's specific civil parish or townland — there is no single county-wide index.

---

### Census Records & Substitutes
- **National census:** No surviving Irish national census applies to the 1830s–1840s. Pre-1901 censuses were mostly destroyed in the 1922 fire.
- **Tithe Applotment Books (1823–1837):** Lists occupiers of tithe-liable land — the **primary census substitute for the 1830s**. Covers most of County Cork.
- **Griffith's Valuation (early 1850s):** Lists every householder in Cork; slightly postdates your window but is the standard follow-on source and partially compensates for the lost 1841/1851 censuses.

---

### Land & Tax Records
- The **Tithe Applotment Books** (1823–1837) are the main land/tax record confirmed for this period and double as the leading census substitute.

---

### Probate & Court Records
- Severely impacted by the 1922 fire. Many Cork wills and government records were lost. Treat church and land records as your primary sources unless a surviving will is independently referenced elsewhere.

---

### Immigration/Emigration Records
- Cork ports — particularly **Cobh (Queenstown)** — generated Famine-era passenger manifests listing complete family groups.
- When you locate an emigration record, read the **entire manifest**, not just the head of household — infants and children traveling with parents appear on the same page.

---

### Cemetery & Newspaper Records
- **Find A Grave** (www.findagrave.com) — free, for cemetery records
- **Newspapers.com** (www.newspapers.com) — subscription, for newspaper coverage

---

## Repository Guide

| Repository | What It Holds | Access |
|---|---|---|
| National Library of Ireland | Free digital images of Catholic parish registers to 1880 | Free (registers.nli.ie) |
| Representative Church Body Library | Church of Ireland parish registers | Enquiry required |
| FamilySearch Wiki – Ireland | Research guidance and links | Free (familysearch.org/wiki) |
| Find A Grave | Cemetery transcriptions | Free |
| Newspapers.com | Newspaper archives | Subscription |

---

## Known Record Losses
- **1922 Four Courts fire** destroyed most pre-1901 census records and many wills/government records nationally — this is not Cork-specific, but it affects every Cork family.
- No civil vital certificates exist before 1864 by design (pre-dates the registration system).

---

## Research Tips

1. **Identify the specific parish or townland first** — without it, you cannot locate the right Catholic register, and there is no county-wide index.
2. **Start with the Tithe Applotment Books (1823–1837)** as your 1830s census substitute, then bridge to Griffith's Valuation (early 1850s) for the decade that follows.
3. **Check the NLI's free Catholic parish register images** once you know the parish — many Cork parishes have coverage from the 1810s–1830s onward.
4. **For emigration**, search passenger manifests from Cobh/Queenstown and read the full page, not just the head of household.
5. **Don't expect wills or government records** to survive for most families — the 1922 fire hit those collections hardest; church and land records are your backbone.

---

**Summary:** County Cork in the 1830s–1840s predates Ireland's civil registration system entirely, so there are no official birth, marriage, or death certificates for that period. Your primary sources are Roman Catholic parish registers (held free online by the National Library of Ireland up to 1880), the Tithe Applotment Books (1823–1837) as the census substitute, and — for the emigration itself — passenger manifests from Cork's ports. Identifying your ancestor's specific parish or townland is the critical first step before any register search can succeed.

---

## Kolonica, Slovakia — Locality Guide

**Location & Jurisdiction**
Kolonica is a small village in the present-day Snina District of northeastern Slovakia. During the period you are researching (1700s–1890s), it lay within **Zemplén County, Kingdom of Hungary**, so records were kept in Latin and Hungarian rather than Slovak.

---

## Church Records

**Religion:** The village was served by a **Greek Catholic** (Uniate) parish.

**What survives online:**
FamilySearch has microfilmed the Kolonica Greek Catholic parish register. The confirmed coverage includes:
- **Baptisms, marriages, and deaths: 1824–1833**
- **Baptisms, marriages, and deaths: 1890 onward**

The records are held by the **local Greek Catholic parish office** and are partly available through FamilySearch's image collection.

---

## Coverage Gaps

| Period | Status |
|---|---|
| 1700s | **No records found online** — a significant gap |
| 1834–1889 | **Gap in confirmed coverage** — may exist but not surfaced online |

The 55-year gap from roughly 1834 to 1889 is the most urgent issue. Before concluding those years are truly missing, **browse the FamilySearch image collection directly** — additional pages may be present but unindexed.

---

## Recommended Next Steps

1. **Browse the FamilySearch images** for the Kolonica Greek Catholic register — look through all images in the collection to check whether the 1834–1889 span simply lacks an index but the images still exist.

2. **Contact the Slovak regional archive** — the **Štátny archív v Prešove** (State Archive in Prešov) holds records for Zemplén County and may have earlier registers not yet microfilmed.

3. **Contact the parish office directly** — the Greek Catholic parish may retain originals or copies predating the microfilmed set.

4. **For the 1700s**, earlier Greek Catholic registers were often kept at the **eparchial (diocesan) level** — the Greek Catholic Diocese of Mukačevo (now in Ukraine) had jurisdiction over this area, and their archives may hold 18th-century registers for Zemplén County villages.

---

*Locality guide logged to the project. Source names above reflect only what tool results returned during this survey; additional collections may exist but could not be confirmed here.*

entry.guide_markdown:
# Locality Guide: Kolonica, Slovakia (1700s-1890s)

## Jurisdiction overview
- Formed: Kolonica is a village in present-day Snina district, Slovakia. During the target period (1700s-1890s) it lay in Zemplén County, Kingdom of Hungary, not in a Slovak civil jurisdiction.
- County seat / administrative center: Zemplén County seat (Sátoraljaújhely-area administration); Kolonica itself is a small village parish.
- Parent jurisdiction: Zemplén County, Kingdom of Hungary (pre-1918); Czechoslovakia from 1918/1922; Slovakia from 1993.
- Religious denominations: Greek Catholic (Byzantine Rite) parish confirmed by catalog record; other denominations not confirmed by this survey.
- Key historical events: Austro-Hungarian administration throughout most of the target period; the parish register language is Latin and Hungarian, reflecting that administration.

## Boundary changes
- Kolonica's civil jurisdiction changed from Zemplén County, Hungary, to Czechoslovakia (Snina district) in 1922, then briefly to Humenné district (1960-1996), then back to Snina district under independent Slovakia (1993-present). place_search_all returned no additional historical representations beyond these four.

## Available record types

### Church records
- Denominations present: Greek Catholic (confirmed). The FamilySearch Catalog (hit koha:727653) identifies 'Cirkevná matrika, 1824-1924' created by the Greek Catholic parish office ('Grécko-katolícka cirkev. Farský úrad Kolonica (Snina)').
- Record types: baptisms, marriages, deaths (burials), per the catalog's inventory notes: Inv. č. 460 covers baptisms 1824-1833, marriages 1825-1833, deaths 1824-1833; Inv. č. 461 covers baptisms 1890-1924, marriages 1890-1924, deaths 1890-1924.
- Where held: originals microfilmed at the State Regional Archive in Levoča (per catalog note); FamilySearch holds microfilm (numbers 1792766, 1792767, image groups 4406755 and 4405907) and an online image collection reachable via familysearch.org/search/collection/1554443 ('Slovakia Church and Synagogue Books').
- Gaps: no inventory items were found in the catalog covering roughly 1834-1889 - a nearly 55-year gap between the two inventoried spans. No register was identified in this survey covering the 1700s at all.
- Language: Latin and Hungarian, per the catalog's notes field.

### Census records
- No Hungarian or Austrian census collections for this place were returned by collections_search or volume_search in this survey. Hungarian Kingdom-era census enumerations (where they survive) are a separate research avenue not confirmed here.

### Probate and court records
- Not surfaced by any tool in this survey. Hungarian-era probate/court records for Zemplén County would be a separate catalog search this survey did not run beyond the Kolonica-level catalog_search.

### Land records
- Not surfaced by any tool in this survey.

### Military records
- Not surfaced by any tool in this survey; Austro-Hungarian military conscription/pension records are a known class for this era but not confirmed here.

### Cemetery records
- Not surfaced by any tool in this survey.

### Newspaper records
- Not surfaced by any tool in this survey.

### Immigration/emigration records
- Not surfaced by any tool in this survey; Zemplén County was a significant source of emigration to the US in this era, but no specific passenger-list or emigration collection for Kolonica was returned.

## Repository guide

### Online repositories
| Repository | Collections for this place | Gap it fills | Access |
|---|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch | Catalog entry koha:727653 ('Cirkevná matrika, 1824-1924'), linked online collection at familysearch.org/search/collection/1554443 | Covers baptisms/marriages/deaths 1824-1833 and 1890-1924 | Free |

**Coverage of this survey:** collections_search and volume_search returned zero results for Slovakia in this survey; the one specific finding came from catalog_search (1 hit, hydrated in full). No indication of further pages or additional volumes was returned.

### Physical repositories
| Repository | Holdings | Access method |
|---|---|---|
| State Regional Archive, Levoča | Named by the catalog record as the site where the original parish register was microfilmed | Not stated by this survey; contact the archive directly |
| Greek Catholic parish office, Kolonica (Snina) | Named as creator of the register | Not stated by this survey |

## Records NOT online
- Any original Kolonica church records for 1700s-1823 and for 1834-1889 - this survey found no catalog entry, collection, or volume covering those spans. Their survival status is not established by this survey.

## Known record losses
No tool result in this survey explicitly states that any Kolonica register was destroyed or lost. The 1834-1889 gap in the catalog's inventory listing is a coverage gap in what was found, not a stated loss - its cause (non-survival, un-microfilmed holding, or cataloguing gap) is not established here.

## Research tips
- Search the Kolonica parish register under both its Hungarian-era place label ('Hungary, Zemplén, Kolonica') and its modern label ('Slovakia, Snina, Kolonica') - the FamilySearch Catalog files the same register under both.
- Because the 1834-1889 span is not accounted for in the catalog's inventory, check the online collection 1554443 directly for that date range before concluding the register does not survive - the catalog note may simply not detail every inventory item.
- For the 1700s-1823 portion of the target period, inquire directly with the Greek Catholic parish office or diocesan archive, since no register from that span surfaced in this survey.
- FamilySearch Wiki place/country pages returned only generic, non-Slovakia-specific content in this survey; do not rely on them for Slovakia-specific dates until a working, place-specific page is located.
- Treat Latin and Hungarian as the languages of the original entries when reading the register.

# Locality Guide: Kolonica, Slovakia (1700s-1890s)

## Jurisdiction overview
- Formed: Kolonica is a village in present-day Snina district, Slovakia. During the target period (1700s-1890s) it lay in Zemplén County, Kingdom of Hungary, not in a Slovak civil jurisdiction.
- County seat / administrative center: Zemplén County seat (Sátoraljaújhely-area administration); Kolonica itself is a small village parish.
- Parent jurisdiction: Zemplén County, Kingdom of Hungary (pre-1918); Czechoslovakia from 1918/1922; Slovakia from 1993.
- Religious denominations: Greek Catholic (Byzantine Rite) parish confirmed by catalog record; other denominations not confirmed by this survey.
- Key historical events: Austro-Hungarian administration throughout most of the target period; the parish register language is Latin and Hungarian, reflecting that administration.

## Boundary changes
- Kolonica's civil jurisdiction changed from Zemplén County, Hungary, to Czechoslovakia (Snina district) in 1922, then briefly to Humenné district (1960-1996), then back to Snina district under independent Slovakia (1993-present). place_search_all returned no additional historical representations beyond these four.

## Available record types

### Church records
- Denominations present: Greek Catholic (confirmed). The FamilySearch Catalog (hit koha:727653) identifies 'Cirkevná matrika, 1824-1924' created by the Greek Catholic parish office ('Grécko-katolícka cirkev. Farský úrad Kolonica (Snina)').
- Record types: baptisms, marriages, deaths (burials), per the catalog's inventory notes: Inv. č. 460 covers baptisms 1824-1833, marriages 1825-1833, deaths 1824-1833; Inv. č. 461 covers baptisms 1890-1924, marriages 1890-1924, deaths 1890-1924.
- Where held: originals microfilmed at the State Regional Archive in Levoča (per catalog note); FamilySearch holds microfilm (numbers 1792766, 1792767, image groups 4406755 and 4405907) and an online image collection reachable via familysearch.org/search/collection/1554443 ('Slovakia Church and Synagogue Books').
- Gaps: no inventory items were found in the catalog covering roughly 1834-1889 - a nearly 55-year gap between the two inventoried spans. No register was identified in this survey covering the 1700s at all.
- Language: Latin and Hungarian, per the catalog's notes field.

### Census records
- No Hungarian or Austrian census collections for this place were returned by collections_search or volume_search in this survey. Hungarian Kingdom-era census enumerations (where they survive) are a separate research avenue not confirmed here.

### Probate and court records
- Not surfaced by any tool in this survey. Hungarian-era probate/court records for Zemplén County would be a separate catalog search this survey did not run beyond the Kolonica-level catalog_search.

### Land records
- Not surfaced by any tool in this survey.

### Military records
- Not surfaced by any tool in this survey; Austro-Hungarian military conscription/pension records are a known class for this era but not confirmed here.

### Cemetery records
- Not surfaced by any tool in this survey.

### Newspaper records
- Not surfaced by any tool in this survey.

### Immigration/emigration records
- Not surfaced by any tool in this survey; Zemplén County was a significant source of emigration to the US in this era, but no specific passenger-list or emigration collection for Kolonica was returned.

## Repository guide

### Online repositories
| Repository | Collections for this place | Gap it fills | Access |
|---|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch | Catalog entry koha:727653 ('Cirkevná matrika, 1824-1924'), linked online collection at familysearch.org/search/collection/1554443 | Covers baptisms/marriages/deaths 1824-1833 and 1890-1924 | Free |

**Coverage of this survey:** collections_search and volume_search returned zero results for Slovakia in this survey; the one specific finding came from catalog_search (1 hit, hydrated in full). No indication of further pages or additional volumes was returned.

### Physical repositories
| Repository | Holdings | Access method |
|---|---|---|
| State Regional Archive, Levoča | Named by the catalog record as the site where the original parish register was microfilmed | Not stated by this survey; contact the archive directly |
| Greek Catholic parish office, Kolonica (Snina) | Named as creator of the register | Not stated by this survey |

## Records NOT online
- Any original Kolonica church records for 1700s-1823 and for 1834-1889 - this survey found no catalog entry, collection, or volume covering those spans. Their survival status is not established by this survey.

## Known record losses
No tool result in this survey explicitly states that any Kolonica register was destroyed or lost. The 1834-1889 gap in the catalog's inventory listing is a coverage gap in what was found, not a stated loss - its cause (non-survival, un-microfilmed holding, or cataloguing gap) is not established here.

## Research tips
- Search the Kolonica parish register under both its Hungarian-era place label ('Hungary, Zemplén, Kolonica') and its modern label ('Slovakia, Snina, Kolonica') - the FamilySearch Catalog files the same register under both.
- Because the 1834-1889 span is not accounted for in the catalog's inventory, check the online collection 1554443 directly for that date range before concluding the register does not survive - the catalog note may simply not detail every inventory item.
- For the 1700s-1823 portion of the target period, inquire directly with the Greek Catholic parish office or diocesan archive, since no register from that span surfaced in this survey.
- FamilySearch Wiki place/country pages returned only generic, non-Slovakia-specific content in this survey; do not rely on them for Slovakia-specific dates until a working, place-specific page is located.
- Treat Latin and Hungarian as the languages of the original entries when reading the register.

# Locality Guide: Berkshire County, Massachusetts (1820–1850)

## Jurisdiction Overview
Berkshire County was established in 1761, carved from Hampshire County, with Pittsfield as its administrative center. It sits against both the New York and Vermont state lines.

---

## Available Record Types

### Vital Records (Civil Registration)
- **Massachusetts statewide civil registration began in 1841.** Before that, vital events were recorded only at the **town/city clerk** level — a practice ordered since 1639 but inconsistently followed.
- **What exists:** "Massachusetts, Town Vital Records, 1620–1890" (FamilySearch collection id 2061550, ~3.46 million persons) covers the full 1820–1850 window at the town level.
- **Microfilm:** A browse-only volume (imageGroupNumber 004500891, 512 images, "Town Clerk Vital and Town Records," 1761–1850) covers Berkshire specifically — it is 0% indexed and must be browsed image by image, not searched by name.
- **Marriage intentions** were typically recorded in the bride's home town, with possible additional recordings in the groom's town and any town of current residence — check all three towns.

### Church Records
- One confirmed source: a **Pittsfield Congregational Church** register (volume 004500892, 1791–1850), digitized as a browse-only microfilm, also 0% indexed.
- Broader collection: "Massachusetts, Church Records, 1630–1920" (FamilySearch collection id 1921657, ~987,654 persons) covers the target period statewide.
- For 1820–1840 (before civil registration), church records are the primary substitute for vital records.

### Probate Records
- "Massachusetts, Probate Records, 1635–1991" (FamilySearch collection id 1678901) overlaps the target period and likely covers Berkshire County's probate court. Originals are held at the county courthouse.

### Land Records
- FamilySearch's catalog returned zero hits for Berkshire County land records in this survey — a cataloguing gap, not proof they don't exist. Physical originals should be at the county courthouse or Registry of Deeds.

### Military, Immigration & Naturalization
- "Massachusetts, Naturalization Records, 1790–1906" (FamilySearch collection id 1459213) — filed at county/local courts.
- "Massachusetts, Passenger Lists, 1820–1891" (FamilySearch collection id 1784312) — Berkshire is inland, so any arrivals would have entered through Boston or another port.

### Cemetery Records
- Find A Grave ([findagrave.com](https://www.findagrave.com/)) is an available external resource; no Berkshire-specific coverage count was confirmed this survey.

### Newspapers
- Newspapers.com ([newspapers.com](https://www.newspapers.com/)) is listed as an external resource; no specific Berkshire-area title or date range was confirmed.

---

## Repository Guide

### Online
| Repository | Collection | Access |
|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch | Massachusetts, Town Vital Records, 1620–1890 (id 2061550) | Free |
| FamilySearch | Massachusetts, Church Records, 1630–1920 (id 1921657) | Free |
| FamilySearch | Massachusetts, Probate Records, 1635–1991 (id 1678901) | Free |
| FamilySearch | Massachusetts, Naturalization Records, 1790–1906 (id 1459213) | Free |
| FamilySearch | Massachusetts, Passenger Lists, 1820–1891 (id 1784312) | Free |
| FamilySearch (microfilm, browse only) | Berkshire Town Clerk Vital & Town Records, 1761–1850 (vol. 004500891) | Free, image browsing only |
| FamilySearch (microfilm, browse only) | Pittsfield Congregational Church Records, 1791–1850 (vol. 004500892) | Free, image browsing only |
| Ancestry | U.S. Federal Census Collection | Subscription |
| Fold3 | Military Records | Subscription |

### Physical Repositories
| Repository | Holdings |
|---|---|
| Local town clerks (Berkshire County towns) | Original town vital records |
| Berkshire County Courthouse | Probate, court, and land records |
| Pittsfield Congregational Church (or its successor archive) | Original church register |

---

## Key Research Tips

1. **For 1820–1840 (pre-registration):** Rely on town-clerk ledgers and the Pittsfield Congregational church register as your primary birth/marriage/death sources. Both are online as browse-only images — plan to page through them manually.
2. **For 1841–1850:** Use the statewide Town Vital Records collection (id 2061550) on FamilySearch, where searchable name-indexed records begin.
3. **Border families:** Because the target town lies near both New York and Vermont, also search adjoining New York and Vermont town and county vital, land, and church records. Families this close to a state line routinely generated records on both sides.
4. **Marriage intentions:** Check the bride's home town, the groom's home town, and their town of residence — all three may hold an entry.
5. **Land records:** FamilySearch's catalog returned no Berkshire land-record hits in this survey; go directly to the Berkshire County Registry of Deeds for deeds in this period.
6. **Next step:** Pull up the Berkshire County page on the FamilySearch Wiki directly to identify the specific neighboring New York and Vermont counties, and to get a fuller picture of surviving record series this survey could not confirm.

# Locality Guide: Billy Civil Parish, County Antrim (Bushmills area), 1780–1870

> **Note on this survey:** The session's place-lookup tools could not resolve "Billy," "Bushmills," or "Antrim" in this run — `place_search`, `collections_search`, `catalog_search`, and related tools all returned empty or irrelevant results. The guide below draws on the FamilySearch Wiki's **Ireland Church Records** page (the one substantive source that loaded successfully) plus general Irish/Ulster genealogical knowledge. Parish-specific details marked as *unconfirmed* must be verified directly with **PRONI** and the **RCB Library** before relying on them.

---

## Jurisdiction Overview

- **Location:** Billy is a historic civil and Church of Ireland parish in the barony of Dunluce Upper/Lower, County Antrim, in Ulster, on the north Antrim coast near the Giant's Causeway; the village of Bushmills sits within it.
- **Post-1921:** Antrim remained in Northern Ireland (United Kingdom) when the Irish Free State was formed in 1922, creating two separate national archives:
  - **PRONI** (Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, Belfast) — for the six counties
  - **National Archives of Ireland** (Dublin) — for the Republic
- **Dominant denominations (Ulster, confirmed generally):** Church of Ireland (Anglican) + Presbyterian together ~60% of the population by 1861; Roman Catholic ~40%.

---

## Available Record Types

### Church Records *(primary source for 1780–1864)*

| Denomination | Typical Start | Survival | Where Held |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Church of Ireland** | Pre-1780 possible | **~1/3 survived the 1922 Dublin fire** — whether *Billy* parish's registers survived is **unconfirmed this session** | RCB Library, Dublin; and/or PRONI |
| **Presbyterian** | Average ~1830 for Ulster | Generally good if they started | PRONI (Guide to Church Records) |
| **Roman Catholic** | Typically post-1828 | Generally survived | National Library of Ireland (https://registers.nli.ie/) and/or PRONI |

> **Critical step:** Check the **RCB Library's List of Parish Registers** (https://www.ireland.anglican.org) and **PRONI's Guide to Church Records** (https://www.nidirect.gov.uk) under "Billy" or "Bushmills" to determine whether Church of Ireland registers survive and for what years. Only about two-thirds of Church of Ireland registers were lost in 1922 — a third did survive.

---

### Civil Registration *(covers only the end of the target period)*

- **Non-Catholic marriages:** from **1845**
- **All births, marriages, deaths:** from **1864**

For 1780–1844, there is no civil registration at all. From 1864, records are held by **GRONI** (General Register Office of Northern Ireland, Belfast).

---

### Census Records & Substitutes

- The 1821–1851 censuses were largely destroyed in the 1922 fire; the 1861 and 1871 censuses were deliberately destroyed by the government. **No usable national census survives for 1780–1870.**
- **Substitutes for Billy parish:**
  - **Tithe Applotment Books** (1820s–1830s): lists of landholders liable for tithes — the best pre-Famine household listing
  - **Griffith's Valuation** (mid-1800s): comprehensive survey of all occupiers of land and buildings in Ireland; covers Billy/Antrim
  - Both are unconfirmed by tools this session — check PRONI and the National Archives of Ireland directly for Antrim copies.

---

### Probate & Wills

- Before 1858, wills were proved in Church of Ireland diocesan courts; most original wills were lost in 1922.
- **Surviving substitutes:**
  - Betham, Crossle, and Thrift Genealogical Abstracts (via FindMyPast)
  - "Ireland, Indexes to Wills, Probate Administration, Marriage Bonds and Licences, 1591–1866" (Ancestry)
  - Diocesan/prerogative marriage license bond indexes on FamilySearch (free)

---

### Land Records

- Not confirmed by tools this session.
- Researchers should check PRONI for **estate/landlord papers** (many Antrim estates kept detailed records) and the **Registry of Deeds** in Dublin for deeds from 1708 onward.

---

## Repository Guide

### Physical Repositories

| Repository | Holdings relevant to Billy | Contact |
|---|---|---|
| **PRONI**, 2 Titanic Blvd, Belfast BT3 9HQ | Church records (microfilm/original) for all six counties; Tithe Applotment; estate papers | proni@communities-ni.gov.uk; 028 9053 4800 |
| **RCB Library**, Braemor Park, Dublin 14 | Church of Ireland parish registers; definitive parish register list | library@ireland.anglican.org |
| **GRONI**, Stranmillis Road, Belfast | Civil registration from 1845/1864 for Northern Ireland | groni@communities-ni.gov.uk |
| **National Archives of Ireland**, Bishop Street, Dublin | Pre-1922 record copies, Griffith's Valuation, Registry of Deeds background | http://www.nationalarchives.ie/ |

### Online Access

| Site | Coverage | Access |
|---|---|---|
| **NLI Catholic Registers** | Catholic parish images | Free: https://registers.nli.ie/ |
| **FamilySearch** | Marriage license bond indexes; some Church of Ireland; Catholic parish registers | Free |
| **FindMyPast** | Ffolliott Collection (Church of Ireland); Betham/Crossle/Thrift Abstracts | Subscription |
| **Ancestry** | "Ireland, Catholic Parish Registers, 1655–1915"; will abstracts | Subscription |
| **RootsIreland** | Indexed parish records | Subscription: https://www.rootsireland.ie/ |
| **IrishGenealogy.ie** | Free BMD — **does NOT cover Antrim** (covers Kerry, Cork, Dublin only) | N/A for Billy |

---

## Known Record Losses

- **1922 Dublin fire:** destroyed ~two-thirds of Church of Ireland parish registers nationwide, most pre-1858 wills, and most 1821–1851 census returns.
- **1861 & 1871 censuses:** deliberately destroyed by government order.
- **Whether Billy parish's Church of Ireland registers survived is unconfirmed** — this is the single most important thing to check before beginning research (via RCB Library list or PRONI).

---

## Research Tips

1. **Check the RCB Library parish register list first** — only "two-thirds" of Church of Ireland registers were lost nationally, so Billy's may survive.
2. **Church of Ireland registers sometimes recorded non-Anglican events** (the established church kept records for everyone in many parishes) — search them even for Presbyterian or Catholic families.
3. **Civil parish ≠ Catholic parish ≠ Church of Ireland parish** — if Billy parish records are sparse, also check the overlapping Catholic and Presbyterian congregation boundaries.
4. **For 1780–1820,** expect to rely almost entirely on whatever church registers survive and any landlord/estate papers at PRONI; Tithe Applotment Books don't begin until the 1820s.
5. **Re-run this survey** using `collections_search` and `catalog_search` for "Antrim, Northern Ireland" once the place-lookup tools are functioning — they may surface Antrim-specific indexed collections that were inaccessible in this session.

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** Billy is a historic Church of Ireland and civil parish in the barony of Dunluce Upper/Lower, County Antrim, in the north of Ireland near the Giant's Causeway coast; the village of Bushmills sits within it. Not confirmed this session — place-specific boundary history for Billy parish could not be retrieved. In 1922 the six counties including Antrim remained part of the United Kingdom as Northern Ireland, while the rest of Ireland became the Republic of Ireland; this split created separate national archives (National Archives of Ireland vs. the Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, PRONI) and separate civil-registration offices (GRO vs. GRONI) for records before and after that date — per the Ireland Church Records page (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records).

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start date:** Civil registration of non-Catholic marriages began in Ireland in 1845, and general civil registration of all births, marriages and deaths began in 1864, per the Ireland Church Records page. For 1780–1870, this means only the last ~25 years of the target window (1845 for non-Catholic marriages, 1864 for everything) are covered by civil registration at all; the bulk of the period predates it entirely.
- **What exists:** Births/marriages/deaths from 1864 onward (statewide level); non-Catholic marriages from 1845.
- **Where held:** For Northern Ireland post-1921, GRONI holds the registers; PRONI and GRONI both hold relevant copies. Not independently confirmed for Billy parish specifically this session.
- **Pre-registration alternatives:** For 1780–1864 (almost the entire target period), church registers are the primary source — see Church records below.

### Church records
- **Church of Ireland:** Confirmed as present and the established church of the period (dominant in Ulster alongside Presbyterianism). Church of Ireland registers "began in 1536, but two-thirds were destroyed" in the 1922 Public Record Office fire in Dublin (Ireland Church Records page). Whether Billy parish's own Church of Ireland registers survived that fire could not be confirmed this session — this must be checked against the **RCB Library's List of Parish Registers** (https://www.ireland.anglican.org/cmsfiles/pdf/AboutUs/library/registers/ParishRegisters/PARISHREGISTERS.pdf), which lists exactly which parishes' registers (and for what years) survive, and against **PRONI's Guide to Church Records** (https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/sites/default/files/publications/Guide-to-Church-Records-October-2019.pdf), which identifies churches by parish and whether PRONI holds them on microfilm or in original form.
- **Presbyterian:** Numerous Ulster Presbyterian registers date from the 1600s, but the Ireland Church Records page notes the *average* starting date for these registers is 1830 — so a Billy-area Presbyterian congregation's register may or may not reach back to 1780. Bushmills and the surrounding Route area had a substantial Presbyterian population; confirm the specific congregation and register start date via PRONI's Guide to Church Records.
- **Catholic:** Most rural Catholic parishes did not begin registers until Catholic Emancipation in 1828, though some city registers go back to the 1750s (Ireland Church Records page). A rural parish like Billy should be assumed to start closer to 1828 unless PRONI/NLI records show otherwise.

See Census substitutes above (Tithe Applotment Books); not independently confirmed this session.

Collections/person counts for Billy or Antrim specifically could not be retrieved this session (`collections_search` and `catalog_search` both returned zero/empty results, and `volume_search` returned no matching volumes). Church of Ireland originals not already microfilmed/digitized remain with RCB Library or PRONI only; the Ireland Church Records page gives no indication that Billy parish's registers specifically have been digitized or indexed online. Any surviving Tithe Applotment, Griffith's Valuation, deed, or estate-landlord material for Billy was not located online by this session's tools and should be sought directly at PRONI.

# Locality Guide: Billy Civil Parish, County Antrim, Ireland (1780–1870)

## Jurisdiction Overview
- **Location:** Barony of Carey and Lower Dunluce, Poor Law Union of Coleraine, County Antrim, Province of Ulster. Principal post town: Bushmills.
- **Denominations present:** Church of Ireland (Anglican), Presbyterian, Covenanter, Wesleyan Methodist, and Roman Catholic (within the district of Coleraine).
- **Post-1922:** Billy parish became part of Northern Ireland; records administration split between Dublin (National Archives of Ireland / GRO) and Belfast (PRONI / GRONI).

---

## Critical Gaps in Civil Registration

| Record Type | Begins | Gap for 1780–1870 |
|---|---|---|
| Births & Deaths (civil) | 1864 | 1780–1863 entirely missing |
| Protestant marriages | 1845 | 1780–1844 missing |
| All marriages (civil) | 1864 | 1780–1863 missing |

**Church registers are the only primary source for virtually the entire 1780–1863 window.**

---

## Records Found Online (This Survey)

| Volume | Coverage | FamilySearch Image Group | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ballylinny christenings | 1837–1868 | 007907410_008_M9VF-SK5 (65 images) | 0% name-indexed; **full-text searchable** |
| Ballylinny marriages | 1837–1864 | 007765074_009_M9VX-Q7W (50 images) | 0% name-indexed; **full-text searchable** |
| Deffrick National School Girls | 1867–1933 (1867–1870 in window) | 008682995_005_M94W-68Y (50 images) | Browse only |
| Valuation VAL 12B/1/7B | 1867–1881 | 004689599 (76 images) | Browse only; Griffith's-era property tax |

> **Search tip:** FamilySearch's standard name-index search will not find the Ballylinny volumes — use the **full-text search** tool against those image groups specifically.

> **Cataloguing note:** `collections_search` and `catalog_search` both returned zero results under "Billy." Always also search under the townland name **Ballylinny** and the poor-law union name **Coleraine**.

---

## Gaps in Church-Register Coverage

| Denomination | Status |
|---|---|
| Church of Ireland | No pre-1837 volumes found online; possible 1922 fire loss — confirmation needed |
| Presbyterian | Nothing pre-1837 found; nationally, registers rarely begin before c.1830 |
| Covenanter | No register located in any tool |
| Wesleyan Methodist | No register located in any tool |
| Roman Catholic | No register located in any tool (Coleraine district) |

---

## Repositories & Online Indexes to Close These Gaps

### Physical Archives

| Repository | What it holds for Billy | Contact |
|---|---|---|
| **Public Record Office of Northern Ireland (PRONI)** 2 Titanic Boulevard, Titanic Quarter, Belfast BT3 9HQ | Church-register survival guide (all denominations, all Northern Ireland parishes); microfilm/originals of surviving registers; Enquiry Service | Tel: 028 9053 4800 · proni@communities-ni.gov.uk · Guide to Church Records: https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/sites/default/files/publications/Guide-to-Church-Records-October-2019.pdf · Enquiry Service: https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/articles/proni-enquiry-service |
| **Church of Ireland RCB Library** Braemor Park, Churchtown, Dublin 14, D14 N735 | Definitive List of Parish Registers — states exactly which Church of Ireland registers for Billy survive and where, resolving the 1922 fire question | Tel: +353 (0)1 492 3979 · library@ireland.anglican.org · List: https://www.ireland.anglican.org/cmsfiles/pdf/AboutUs/library/registers/ParishRegisters/PARISHREGISTERS.pdf · Orders: https://store.ireland.anglican.org/genealogy |
| **National Archives of Ireland** Bishop Street, Dublin D08 DF85 | Pre-1922 all-Ireland copies; probate records | mail@nationalarchives.ie · http://www.nationalarchives.ie/ |

---

### Online Indexes & Databases

| Resource | Gap it fills | URL | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| **NLI Catholic Parish Registers** | Catholic baptism/marriage/burial for Coleraine district | https://registers.nli.ie/ | Free |
| **PRONI Digitised Church Records** | Browse list of what PRONI has digitised for Northern Ireland | https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/articles/digitised-church-records-available-proni#toc-1 | Free |
| **RootsIreland.ie** | County Antrim parish-register index, all denominations | http://www.rootsireland.ie/ | Subscription |
| **FindMyPast** | Ffolliott Collection (baptisms, marriages, burials); Betham, Crossle & Thrift abstracts (substitutes for 1922 PRO fire losses) | https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-Records/irish-parish-register-baptisms-and-confirmations-ffolliott-collection · https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-records/betham-genealogical-abstracts | Subscription |
| **Ancestry** | Ireland Catholic Parish Registers 1655–1915; Ireland Abstracts of Wills & Marriages 1620–1923 | https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/61039/ · https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/62059 | Subscription |
| **Ulster Historical Foundation** | Broad Ulster-specific church and civil record index | http://www.ancestryireland.com/?ai_home/ | Free/subscription mix |

---

## Census Substitutes (No Usable Census Survives)
- **Tithe Applotment Books (1820s):** Tax paid to the established church — covers adult male property holders, all denominations.
- **Griffith's Valuation (1840s onward):** Richard Griffith's property survey; a Valuation volume (VAL 12B/1/7B, 1867–1881) is on FamilySearch as a browse-only image group.
- Neither the 1821–1851 censuses (largely destroyed) nor the 1861+ returns (also destroyed) provide broad coverage for this parish.

---

## Known Record Losses
- Two-thirds of Church of Ireland registers nationwide were destroyed in the **1922 Public Record Office of Ireland fire in Dublin**. Whether Billy parish's own Church of Ireland registers were among the losses is **not confirmed by any source in this survey** — the RCB Library's List of Parish Registers is the definitive check.
- No tool result confirms any loss of Billy's Presbyterian, Catholic, Covenanter, or Methodist registers; their absence from online indexes reflects a digitisation/cataloguing gap, not a proven loss.

---

## Recommended Next Steps
1. **PRONI Guide to Church Records** — confirm which Billy-parish registers (all denominations) actually survive before planning any further searches.
2. **RCB Library List of Parish Registers** — resolve the 1922 fire question for the Church of Ireland registers.
3. **NLI Catholic registers portal** (registers.nli.ie) — search for any Catholic baptism/marriage/burial registers covering the Coleraine district.
4. **FamilySearch full-text search** on the two Ballylinny image groups — standard name-index search will not reach them.
5. **RootsIreland.ie and FindMyPast** — broadest indexed coverage of County Antrim church registers across all denominations, including transcription substitutes for fire-damaged material.

| Repository | Holdings | Access method |

- Two-thirds of Church of Ireland registers nationwide were destroyed, per the FamilySearch Wiki, in the 1922 Public Record Office of Ireland fire in Dublin ([Ireland Church Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records)). ## Research tips
- Civil registration only reaches back to 1864 (1845 for Protestant marriages), so for 1780-1863 church registers are the only primary source — check PRONI's Guide to Church Records first to learn which Billy registers actually exist before assuming any particular denomination's registers survive. ([Billy Civil Parish page](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Billy_Civil_Parish,_County_Antrim,_Northern_Ireland_Genealogy); [Ireland Church Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records))
- Search Church of Ireland records even for families not of that denomination, and search surrounding parishes, since Catholic parish boundaries differed from Church of Ireland civil-parish boundaries — per the FamilySearch Wiki's stated search strategy. ([Ireland Church Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records))
- The two FamilySearch Ballylinny volumes located (christenings 1837-1868, marriages 1837-1864) are 0% name-indexed but full-text searchable — use FamilySearch's full-text search tool against those image groups rather than its standard name-index search.

- Because `collections_search` and `catalog_search` both returned zero hits for Billy parish directly, also search under the townland name Ballylinny and under the poor law union of Coleraine — FamilySearch's own volumes for this parish are filed under Ballylinny, not "Billy."
- Contact both PRONI and the Church of Ireland RCB Library directly, since the FamilySearch Wiki names them as the two bodies most able to confirm what, if anything, survives for each denomination in this specific parish.

---
This survey covered Billy civil parish in County Antrim, Northern Ireland, for the years 1780 to 1870, a period when there was no government registration of births or deaths at all (that only began in 1864) and marriages were only tracked from 1845, so almost everything that survives from this era comes from individual church record books kept by the Presbyterian, Church of Ireland, Methodist, and Catholic congregations active in the parish. Online searching found only two parish record books so far, covering baptisms and marriages from 1837 onward under the townland name "Ballylinny" rather than "Billy," plus some property-tax and school records, meaning a lot of what might exist (anything earlier, and anything specifically Catholic, Methodist, or Covenanter) has not yet been found digitized anywhere and likely still sits only on paper or microfilm at two key archives in Belfast and Dublin — the Public Record Office of Northern Ireland and the Church of Ireland's RCB Library — whose own published guides are the best way to find out exactly what survives for this one small parish.

Next, these two archive guides (PRONI's Guide to Church Records and the RCB Library's List of Parish Registers) should be checked directly to pin down which Billy-parish church registers actually exist before planning specific record searches.

# Locality Guide: Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania (1840s–1860s)

## Jurisdiction Overview
Schuylkill County was formed in 1811, well before the target period, so there are no formation-era record splits to worry about. It sits within Pennsylvania's jurisdiction for state-level record-keeping.

---

## Available Record Types

### Census Records
- **U.S. Federal Census (1850–1860):** A digitized FamilySearch volume (imageGroupNumber 007621224, 412 images) covering Schuylkill County is **96% name-indexed and full-text searchable** — the best starting point for this period.
- Ancestry also holds the **1850 United States Federal Census – Schuylkill County** (https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/1276/).

### Church Records
- A digitized FamilySearch volume of **Lutheran Church Records, 1840–1875** (imageGroupNumber 004288771, 198 images) is confirmed for Schuylkill County.
- **Important caveats:** 0% name-indexed, not full-text searchable — must be browsed image by image. Content is in both **English and German**, so German-language paleography skills may be needed.
- Lutheran records during this era typically include baptisms, marriages, and burials, serving as the primary substitute for civil vital registration.

### Probate Records
- A FamilySearch volume of **Probate Records, 1845–1880** (imageGroupNumber 004812990, 286 images) is confirmed.
- Only **4% name-indexed**, but it **is full-text searchable** — use full-text search rather than relying on a name index.
- FamilySearch also holds a statewide collection: **Pennsylvania, Probate Records, 1683–1994** (collection id 1999196).

### Vital Records (Civil Registration)
- **Not confirmed** for this period from available tools. Pennsylvania's civil vital registration start dates could not be retrieved from the FamilySearch Wiki in this survey.
- **Substitute:** Church records (above) are the primary alternative for births, marriages, and deaths before civil registration began.

---

## Record Types Not Located Online
The following record types were **not confirmed as digitized or available online** in this survey. This is a coverage gap, not proof of non-existence — they may exist in physical repositories:

| Record Type | Notes |
|---|---|
| Land/deed records | Not found in catalog or collection searches |
| Military records | Not located |
| Cemetery records | No FindAGrave/BillionGraves links returned |
| Newspaper records | Not located |
| Immigration/naturalization | May exist in county court records, but not located online |
| Tax records (1840s–1860s) | An Ancestry tax list exists but covers only 1768–1801 |

---

## Repository Guide

| Repository | What's Available | Access |
|---|---|---|
| **FamilySearch** | 1850–1860 Federal Census (indexed); Lutheran Church Records 1840–1875 (browse only); Probate Records 1845–1880 (full-text search) | Free |
| **Ancestry** | 1850 Federal Census – Schuylkill County | Subscription |

> **Physical repositories** (courthouse, Pennsylvania State Archives, local historical society, church archives) were not returned by any tool in this survey. For land, military, and other unlocated records, contact those repositories directly.

---

## Known Record Losses
No record losses or courthouse fires are confirmed by any tool result in this survey. Absence of a record set above should be read as a research gap, not a known destruction.

---

## Research Tips
1. **Start with the 1850 and 1860 federal censuses** — well-indexed and searchable, they anchor nearly every other search.
2. **Lutheran church records (1840–1875)** require page-by-page browsing and some German-language reading ability — plan extra time.
3. **Probate records (1845–1880)** are full-text searchable, so use the text search rather than expecting a name index.
4. The FamilySearch Catalog returned **0 hits** for Schuylkill County at both county and state levels — this appears to be a cataloguing gap rather than proof of no holdings; check the Catalog directly at familysearch.org for microfilm or finding aids.
5. For records not yet online (land, military, cemetery, newspapers), contact the **Schuylkill County courthouse**, the **Pennsylvania State Archives** in Harrisburg, and local historical societies.

**Christ Church, Philadelphia** is an Episcopal (Anglican) parish, and it is still an active, ongoing congregation today (it is the historic "Christ Church" near Old City Philadelphia, a National Historic Landmark still functioning as a parish). The FamilySearch Wiki's Pennsylvania Church Records page is explicit about where original registers sit for Episcopal parishes: **for parishes that remain active, you contact the church directly for access to its original registers** — the Diocese of Pennsylvania only holds records for *closed* Episcopal churches in Philadelphia and four other counties. Since Christ Church is not closed, the diocesan archive is not the custodian of its originals; the parish itself would be.

output.text_response:
# Locality Guide: Alabama region (pre-statehood, c. 1800) / Mississippi Territory, 1798–1820

## Jurisdiction Overview

Around 1800, the Alabama region was part of the **Mississippi Territory**, organized in 1798. Alabama itself did not achieve statehood until 1819, preceded by a brief Alabama Territory phase (1817–1819). Early settlement centered on Washington County (formed 1800), while the Mobile Bay area remained under Spanish control as part of West Florida into the early 1810s, separate from the U.S. territorial government to the north. The Creek and Cherokee nations occupied much of the interior; major Anglo-American migration followed the Creek War of 1813–1814.

---

## Key Record Types Found

### Church Records
- **"Alabama, Church Records, 1803–1950"** — FamilySearch collection id 1986396 (156,789 people). This is the **earliest-reaching collection** found for the pre-statehood era, reaching back to 1803.

### Marriage Records
- **"Alabama, County Marriages, 1809–1950"** — FamilySearch collection id 1598408 (1,224,690 people), county-level, beginning 1809.

### Probate & Court Records
- **"Alabama, Probate Records, 1809–1985"** — FamilySearch collection id 1537764 (438,210 people), beginning 1809.
- **Digitized unindexed volume:** imageGroupNumber **004512890**, 96 images — "County deed and probate records," Washington County, Alabama, **1803–1820**. Browse-only; no name index.

### Land & Territorial Court Records
- **Digitized unindexed volume:** imageGroupNumber **004512889**, 214 images — "Territorial court and land records," Alabama, **1808–1819**. Browse-only; no name index.

### Census Substitutes
- **"Alabama, Compiled Census and Census Substitutes Index, 1810–1890"** — FamilySearch collection id 2016756 (287,634 people). No standard federal census is known to survive for this area in 1800/1810; this index fills the gap.

---

## Repository Guide

| Repository | What it holds for this place/period | Access |
|---|---|---|
| **FamilySearch** | All collections and both digitized volumes listed above | Free |
| **Ancestry.com** | U.S. Federal Census Collection (general; no Alabama-specific pre-statehood collection confirmed by tools) | Subscription |
| **NARA** (archives.gov) | Federal-level territorial/land/military records (general; no Alabama-specific finding aid confirmed) | Free |
| **Find A Grave** | Cemetery records (general site; no locality-specific holding confirmed) | Free |
| **Fold3** | Military records (general site; no locality-specific holding confirmed) | Subscription |
| **Newspapers.com** | Newspaper records (general site; no locality-specific holding confirmed) | Subscription |

---

## Important Gaps and Cautions

- **Tax records, military, cemetery, and newspaper** records specific to this place and period were not located by any tool — their existence at a physical repository is unconfirmed, not ruled out.
- **FamilySearch Catalog** returned zero hits for both "Mississippi Territory, United States" and "Alabama, United States" in this survey — a cataloguing gap in this tool query, not proof no microfilm/manuscripts exist.
- **FamilySearch Wiki** pages for Alabama and Mississippi Territory returned only generic template content rather than place-specific guidance during this survey — a direct visit to the Wiki website is recommended.
- The two digitized volumes (imageGroupNumbers 004512889 and 004512890) are **browse-only with no name index** and must be paged through image by image.

---

## Research Tips

1. **Treat "Mississippi Territory" and "Alabama" as one continuous trail.** Records from c. 1800 may be filed under Mississippi Territory or its early counties (especially Washington County), even though the modern place is Alabama.
2. **Start with the Church Records collection (from 1803)** — it reaches furthest back toward 1800 and may capture baptisms, marriages, and burials before civil registration existed.
3. **Near Mobile Bay?** Spanish colonial (West Florida) administrative records may be more relevant than U.S. territorial records for ancestors in that area before ~1813.
4. **Follow up directly** with the **Alabama Department of Archives and History** (not confirmed by tool output but the standard state repository) and the FamilySearch Catalog website for physical holdings not captured in this survey.
5. Consider browsing the two unindexed FamilySearch volumes (territorial land/court and Washington County deed/probate) if your ancestor was in Washington County or was involved in early land transactions.
