# Locality Guide: Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania, anthracite coal region (1860-1900)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** 1811 from Berks and Northampton counties
- **County seat / administrative center:** Pottsville
- **Parent jurisdiction:** Pennsylvania, United States
- **Population during period:** 1860: 89,510; 1870: 116,428; 1880: 129,974; 1900: 172,927 (US Census, via place_population)
- **Economy:** Anthracite coal mining dominated the county from the mid-19th century, drawing large numbers of Irish and other immigrant laborers into collieries and breaker work
- **Ethnic composition:** Irish immigrant mining communities concentrated in coal-patch towns alongside German and, later, Eastern European populations
- **Religious denominations:** Roman Catholic parishes established 1840-1870 to serve Irish and Eastern European immigrants, per the FamilySearch Wiki 'Pennsylvania Coal Region Records' page (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Pennsylvania_Coal_Region_Records)
- **Key historical events:** Growth of anthracite mining industry through the period; a 1903 records consolidation affected survival of company payroll books later compiled into the Lackawanna Valley Anthracite Index

## Boundary changes
- Schuylkill County was formed in 1811 from Berks and Northampton counties (place_search_all) and its boundaries were stable through the 1860-1900 period surveyed.

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start date:** Not confirmed -- the constructed Pennsylvania/Schuylkill Vital_Records wiki URL returned only a generic 'Genealogy_Records' template, not a page naming a specific start date or level; do not assume a date.
- **What exists:** A browse-only Marriage Records volume (imageGroupNumber 007936753) covering 1870-1910, 94 images, 0% indexed, not full-text searchable (volume_search).
- **Where held:** FamilySearch digitized volume, browse-only; underlying originals at the county level (standard PA practice) -- not confirmed by a wiki page for this county.
- **Gaps:** No confirmed civil birth/death records volume was found in this survey for Schuylkill County in this window.
- **Pre-registration alternatives:** Catholic and other church baptismal/burial registers (see Church records below).

### Church records
- **Denominations present:** Roman Catholic parishes founded 1840-1870 for Irish/Eastern European immigrants (FamilySearch Wiki, Pennsylvania Coal Region Records).
- **Record types:** Baptisms, marriages, burials, confirmations (per diocesan custom).
- **Where held:** Before 1868, Diocese of Philadelphia held authority over Schuylkill County parishes; Schuylkill remained with Philadelphia after 1868 (unlike Luzerne/Lackawanna, which moved to the new Diocese of Scranton) until the Diocese of Allentown was erected in 1961 -- so for the 1860s-1890s, Schuylkill parish registers are Philadelphia diocesan records. A browse-only Church Records volume (imageGroupNumber 007936751, 1842-1895, 187 images, languages English and German) is also digitized on FamilySearch, 0% indexed.
- **Gaps:** No full-text or name-indexed coverage; must browse image by image, and some entries are in German.
- **Language:** English and German (per volume_search); Catholic registers are commonly Latin, not confirmed by a tool result here.

### Census records
- **Federal census:** 1850 Schuylkill County census curated externally via Ancestry (https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/1276/); later federal censuses (1860-1900) not separately confirmed in this survey's external-links results.
- **State/provincial census:** None found in this survey.
- **Other enumerations:** Pennsylvania triennial state tax assessments from 1853 list householder, real estate value, occupation, and sometimes nativity (FamilySearch Wiki, Pennsylvania Coal Region Records) -- useful substitute/supplement between censuses.
- **Access:** 1850 census link above is external (Ancestry, subscription); no FamilySearch-indexed Schuylkill census collection was returned by collections_search for this period.

### Probate and court records
- **Types:** Wills, administrations (a county-level Probate Records volume, imageGroupNumber 007936749, 1851-1930, 412 images, 0% indexed, browse-only); also a statewide 'Pennsylvania, Probate Records, 1683-1994' collection (collections_search id 1999196, personCount 0).
- **Testate or intestate:** Not established for Patrick Flynn; search both will and administration series.
- **Date range:** County volume covers 1851-1930, within the research window.
- **Where held:** FamilySearch digitized microfilm (browse-only); statewide collection also on FamilySearch with no indexed persons recorded.

### Land records
- **Survey system:** Not confirmed by a tool result for this county.
- **Land-distribution jurisdiction:** Not confirmed -- no Schuylkill County Land_and_Property wiki page content was returned (only the generic template).
- **Types:** A Deed Records volume (imageGroupNumber 007936752, 1815-1900, 543 images) is 22% name-searchable (recordSearchablePercent), not full-text searchable -- the most indexed record type found for this county.
- **Date range:** 1815-1900 (volume_search).
- **Where held:** FamilySearch digitized volume; originals ordinarily at the county recorder of deeds, not confirmed by a wiki page here.

### Military records
- **Relevant conflicts:** American Civil War (1861-1865) falls within the period; no Schuylkill-specific military collection or volume was returned by this survey's tools.
- **Record types:** Not confirmed for this county in this survey -- consult NARA service/pension records generically.
- **Where held:** National Archives and Records Administration (per the generic FamilySearch guidance retrieved); no specific Schuylkill volume found.

### Cemetery records
- **Major cemeteries:** Not confirmed by a tool result in this survey.
- **Online coverage:** Not confirmed -- no FindAGrave/BillionGraves link for Schuylkill County was returned by external_links_search.
- **Physical records:** Not confirmed.

### Newspaper records
- **Local papers:** Not confirmed by a tool result in this survey.
- **Where held:** Not confirmed.
- **Content value:** Obituaries and marriage notices would be valuable for an Irish mining family but no specific paper or archive was returned here.

### Immigration/emigration records
- **Relevant ports:** Not directly on a port, but Irish immigrants to the anthracite region commonly arrived via Philadelphia or New York; no Schuylkill-specific immigration volume was returned by this survey.
- **Record types:** A browse-only Naturalization Records volume (imageGroupNumber 007936750, 1849-1915, 298 images, 0% indexed) was found for Schuylkill County.
- **Where held:** FamilySearch digitized volume, browse-only.
- **Content note:** When any passenger manifest is found, check the full manifest for all family members, including children.

### Tax records
- **Types:** Pennsylvania state assessors enumerated residents triennially from 1853 (householder, real estate value, occupation, sometimes nativity), per the FamilySearch Wiki Pennsylvania Coal Region Records page; also 'Pennsylvania, U.S., Tax and Exoneration Lists, 1768-1801' curated on Ancestry (https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/7667/), though that collection's date range (to 1801) predates this survey's 1860-1900 window.
- **Date range:** Triennial from 1853 onward per the Coal Region Records page; the Ancestry Tax and Exoneration collection itself ends in 1801 and is out of period.
- **Where held:** State assessment ledgers; access method not confirmed beyond the wiki citation.
- **Substitute value:** Useful between censuses and as an occupation/nativity substitute for Irish mining families.

### Other record types
- **Lackawanna Valley Anthracite Index, 1855-1898:** Names ~41,000 colliery workers across the lower anthracite field from company payroll books, including occupation (loader, breaker boy, mule driver), wage rate, and parish of origin where stated (FamilySearch Wiki, Pennsylvania Coal Region Records). This index is framed around the lower anthracite field (Lackawanna/Luzerne area); its applicability to Schuylkill specifically is not confirmed by the page and should be checked directly.

## Repository guide

### Online repositories
| Repository | Collections for this place | Gap it fills | Access |
|---|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch | Pennsylvania, Schuylkill County Church Records (id SYNTH-PA-CHURCH, 1708-1985); Pennsylvania, Probate Records, 1683-1994 (id 1999196); 5 digitized browse-only/partially-indexed volumes (probate, naturalization, church, deed, marriage) | Fills the gap of no confirmed civil vital-records start date by offering church and probate alternatives | Free |
| Ancestry | Pennsylvania, U.S., Tax and Exoneration Lists, 1768-1801 (https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/7667/); 1850 United States Federal Census - Schuylkill County (https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/1276/) | Fills the 'no FamilySearch-indexed Schuylkill census collection for this period' gap, though the 1850 census itself predates the 1860-1900 window | Subscription |

**Coverage of this survey:** volume_search returned a complete set of 5 digitized volumes for Schuylkill County in this window (complete: true) -- this is the full matched set, not a partial page.

### Physical repositories
| Repository | Holdings | Access method |
|---|---|---|
| Schuylkill County Courthouse (Pottsville) | Original deed, probate, and civil court records (level not independently confirmed by a wiki page) | In-person / mail, per standard PA county practice |
| Archdiocese of Philadelphia Archives | Catholic parish registers for Schuylkill County parishes through the 1860s-1890s (per diocesan boundary noted above) | Contact method not confirmed by this survey |

## Records NOT online
- Civil vital records (if any exist for this county/period) -- no online FamilySearch volume was found covering Schuylkill births or deaths in this window; only a browse-only marriage volume.
- Full text of the Schuylkill church register volume (1842-1895) is online as browse-only images but not searchable by name.
- Cemetery and newspaper records -- no online holdings were confirmed by this survey.

## Known record losses
- No record loss for Schuylkill County specifically was stated by any tool result in this survey. The Lackawanna Valley Anthracite Index page notes that it exists because company payroll books 'survived' a 1903 records consolidation, implying other payroll material did not, but this is stated for the lower anthracite field generally, not pinned to Schuylkill.

## Research tips
- Consult the FamilySearch Wiki's dedicated 'Pennsylvania Coal Region Records' page (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Pennsylvania_Coal_Region_Records) first for anthracite-specific indexes before falling back to generic Pennsylvania vital/church record searches.
- Confirm which diocese held a given Schuylkill parish's registers for the exact research year before requesting records -- jurisdiction follows the 1868 diocesan boundary noted above, not the modern diocese of Allentown (erected 1961).
- Because the county's five digitized FamilySearch volumes are overwhelmingly browse-only (0% indexed on four of five), budget time for image-by-image review rather than relying on name search.
- Search adjoining anthracite counties (Luzerne, Carbon, Northumberland) as well as Schuylkill, since Irish mining families moved between coal patches across county lines; this survey did not retrieve a Neighboring Counties table to name specific adjoining towns.
- Use the 1853-onward triennial Pennsylvania state tax assessments as a census substitute and occupation/nativity source between federal enumerations.
- Treat Schuylkill's own FamilySearch Vital_Records page as unconfirmed; verify any civil-registration date independently before using it in an analysis.

# Locality Guide: Vermont (Pre-Statehood, approx. 1760–1791)

## Jurisdiction Overview

Vermont was not a recognized colonial jurisdiction during this period. The territory was **disputed between the Province of New York and the Province of New Hampshire**, with settlers holding "New Hampshire Grants" that New York refused to recognize. Vermont declared independence in 1777 and operated as the **Vermont Republic** until admission as the 14th U.S. state in 1791. FamilySearch's place system treats Vermont as a jurisdiction only from statehood onward; there is no distinct pre-1791 "Vermont" jurisdiction in that system.

**Key implication:** Because this territory was contested before 1777, records may be filed under New York or New Hampshire colonial administration rather than any "Vermont" record series.

---

## Boundary Changes

- Before 1777/1791, the territory was claimed and granted by both New Hampshire and New York governors.
- No county structure existed in this period — records are organized by **town/proprietorship** and by the competing colonial grant systems, not by county.
- The 1771 New York Grant Survey (see below) is a direct artifact of this contested jurisdiction.

---

## Available Record Types

### Vital Records (Civil Registration)
- **Statewide registration** did not begin until **1857** — well after this period.
- **What exists:** Town clerk records survive unevenly, **some back to the 1770s**, making direct contact with individual town clerks the route into this period.
- **Practical substitutes:** Church/congregational records and town proprietors' records (see below).

### Land Records ⭐ *Primary source for this period*
- The **Vermont 1771 Grant Survey Schedule**, prepared under New York colonial authority, enumerates roughly **1,800 grantees** of the New Hampshire Grants, with:
  - Grantee name
  - Township grant date
  - Acreage
  - Disputed-claim status
- This is the **earliest systematic resident list** identified for the future state.
- Note: This survey found no digitized copy in the FamilySearch Catalog (`catalog_search` returned zero hits) — physical location is not confirmed here.

### Town Histories ⭐ *Key substitute source*
- Nineteenth-century town histories (mostly published **1860–1900**) "often reprint colonial-era proprietors' records that are otherwise difficult to access," per the FamilySearch Wiki's Vermont Genealogy page.
- Use these when original town records cannot be located.

### Church Records
- Church registers generally predate civil registration and are the best substitute for vital records in this period.
- Vermont-specific denomination detail and date ranges were **not confirmed** by this survey's tool results — this is an open gap to investigate further.

### Census Records
- The federal census begins in **1790** — only the very tail end of this period, and Vermont had just been admitted as a state at that point.
- No state or colonial census for 1760–1791 Vermont was found.

### Probate & Court Records
- No county government existed before statehood, so pre-1791 probate matters would have gone through **New York or New Hampshire provincial courts**, or informally at the town/proprietors level.
- Specific holdings for this period were **not confirmed** by this survey.

### Military Records
- The Revolutionary War (1775–1783) falls within this period; Vermont's Green Mountain Boys militia is historically significant.
- Vermont-specific militia or pension holdings were **not confirmed** by this survey's tool results.

---

## Repository Guide

### Online
| Repository | Resource | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch Wiki | [Vermont Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Vermont_Genealogy) | Names the 1771 Grant Survey and town-history substitutes; free |

> **Tool coverage note:** `collections_search`, `volume_search`, and `catalog_search` all returned **zero results** for Vermont in 1760–1791. This reflects a cataloguing/digitization gap for this pre-statehood window — it does not mean the underlying records don't exist.

### Curated External Links (not Vermont-specific)
Returned by the FamilySearch external links tool as general resources: **Ancestry** (U.S. Federal Census), **FamilySearch Wiki** vital records category, **Find A Grave**, **Newspapers.com**, **Fold3**, and **NARA**.

### Physical Repositories
The FamilySearch Wiki implies **individual town clerk offices** hold the earliest surviving town vital records. The Vermont State Archives and Vermont Historical Society (not returned by tool results but historically relevant) would be natural next stops for pre-statehood records.

---

## Records NOT Online (as of this survey)
- Vermont 1771 Grant Survey Schedule
- Pre-1791 town proprietors' records
- Any pre-statehood probate or militia records

None were located in the FamilySearch Catalog or digitized collections.

---

## Research Tips

1. **Don't search for a "Vermont" jurisdiction before 1777.** Search New York and New Hampshire colonial-era land and court records for anything before Vermont's declaration of independence.
2. **Start with the 1771 Grant Survey Schedule** — it's the earliest systematic list of roughly 1,800 residents/grantees in the territory.
3. **Use 19th-century town histories** as surrogates for lost or inaccessible colonial-era proprietors' records.
4. **Contact individual town clerks** for vital records; some survive back to the 1770s, but there is no central repository for this period.
5. **Civil statewide registration begins in 1857** — for births, marriages, and deaths before that, town clerks and church registers are the sources.
6. **The 1790 federal census** is available at the very boundary of this period and can help confirm families present just after statehood.

---

> **Open gaps in this guide:** Vermont-specific church, probate, census, and military record details for 1760–1791 could not be confirmed from the tool results retrieved. Treat those categories as requiring further investigation via the FamilySearch Wiki's Vermont-specific articles and the Vermont State Archives, rather than as confirmed absent.

Here is the locality guide for **Yorkshire, England, 1851**:

---

## Yorkshire, England — Locality Guide for 1851 Death Records

### Civil Registration (Most Important Starting Point)
Civil death registration began across England and Wales on **1 July 1837**, so any death in 1851 should have been officially registered. However, enforcement was uneven in the early decades, so a death may sometimes appear only in church records even after civil registration began.

**Where to search:**
- **FreeBMD** (free) — searchable index of GRO births, marriages, and deaths
- **GRO (General Register Office) website** (gov.uk) — official government index; order a certificate once you find the entry
- **Ancestry** and **Findmypast** (subscription) — also carry the GRO death index

### Church of England Parish Burial Registers
Parish burial registers continued alongside civil registration and sometimes capture deaths that the civil system missed. Yorkshire has extensive, well-preserved parish records, many of them digitized.

**Where to search:**
- FamilySearch, Ancestry, and Findmypast all hold Yorkshire parish register collections
- **Bishop's transcripts** (annual copies of parish registers sent to the diocese) provide a secondary check

### 1851 Census
The census (taken 30 March 1851) can help confirm where the person was living just before their death and verify family details.

### Probate / Wills
If the deceased left an estate, note that the **national probate index begins in 1858** — anything earlier falls under **church-court probate jurisdiction**. Original pre-1858 Yorkshire probate material is held at:
- **Borthwick Institute for Archives**, York

### Important Yorkshire Note — The Three Ridings
Yorkshire was historically divided into the **North Riding, East Riding, and West Riding**. Records are often indexed by Riding rather than simply "Yorkshire," so search all three divisions to avoid missing anything.

### Recommended Next Steps
1. Search the **GRO death index via FreeBMD or the GRO site** for the person's name and approximate death date to obtain a registration district reference.
2. Order the death certificate (or find a transcription) for full details — cause of death, informant, and address.
3. Check the **matching parish burial register** for the same area as a cross-reference.
4. If the name or date is uncertain, the **1851 census** can help confirm place of residence and household members.

> *Note: Some digitized microfilm volume and catalog lookups returned no results during this survey — that reflects a gap in what could be checked here, not an absence of records. Yorkshire's holdings are well documented and widely digitized.*

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** Yorkshire is an ancient county (standardPlace dated +866/+1801 historically, reorganised as 'Yorkshire, England, United Kingdom' from 1801).

- **Start date:** 1 July 1837, nationally (General Register Office level), under the Registration Act 1836 (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/England_Civil_Registration).

- **Pre-registration alternatives:** Church of England burial registers and bishop's transcripts (see Church records).

### Church records
- **Denominations present:** Church of England (established); Nonconformist (Methodist, Baptist, Quaker, etc.) per collections_search title "England and Wales, Non-Conformist Record Indexes (RG4-8), 1588-1977" (collection 1666142).
- **Record types:** Baptisms, marriages, burials; collection 4439317 "England, Yorkshire, Parish Registers, 1538-2016" (27.3 million people) and collection 4319956 "England, Yorkshire, Bishop's Transcripts, 1547-1957" (11.9 million people) both cover 1851.
- **Where held:** FamilySearch digitized collections above; originals at Yorkshire parish churches and diocesan record offices; the Borthwick Institute for Archives, University of York, holds ecclesiastical material (http://www.york.ac.uk/borthwick/, from external_links_search).
- **Language:** English.

- **Federal/national census:** collections_search returned "England and Wales, Census, 1851" (collection 2563939, ~1.57 million indexed people) -- directly in the target year, and useful to corroborate household composition near a death.

- **Access:** Indexed on FamilySearch (collection above); also offered via Ancestry/Findmypast per external_links_search.

- **Testate or intestate:** Both series exist; an 1851 death predates the 1858 national index, so pre-1858 Yorkshire probate (ecclesiastical court records, held at the Borthwick Institute) is the series to search, not the national index.
- **Date range:** Pre-1858 material (Yorkshire collection to 1858) plus the national index from 1858.
- **Where held:** Borthwick Institute for Archives (ecclesiastical courts); national index at FamilySearch/Ancestry from 1858.

### Land records
- Not confirmed by tool results this run; external_links_search returned "West Yorkshire, England, Select Land Tax Records, 1704-1932" (Ancestry) and "West Yorkshire, England Estate Rentals, 1380-1932" (Ancestry), both of which overlap 1851.

- external_links_search returned no FindAGrave/BillionGraves-specific Yorkshire link in this run; "Yorkshire Monumental Inscriptions" (Findmypast) was returned.

- Several Yorkshire-area papers were returned by external_links_search, but the ones with dated ranges mostly start after 1851 (e.g. Yorkshire Gazette 1819-1920 is the one that actually covers 1851) -- useful for an obituary or death notice.

### Immigration/emigration records

### Tax records
- "West Yorkshire, England, Select Land Tax Records, 1704-1932" and "West Yorkshire, England, Select Rate Books, Accounts and Censuses, 1705-1893" (both Ancestry, via external_links_search) overlap 1851.

### Other record types
- "West Yorkshire, England Select Poor Law and Township Records, 1663-1914" (Ancestry) may record pauper deaths/burials not elsewhere documented.

### Online repositories
| Repository | Collections for this place | Gap it fills | Access |
|---|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch | England and Wales Death Registration Index 1837-2007 (2285341); England and Wales Census 1851 (2563939); England, Yorkshire, Parish Registers 1538-2016 (4439317); England, Yorkshire, Bishop's Transcripts 1547-1957 (4319956) | Core death index, census corroboration, parish burial cross-check | Free |

**Coverage of this survey:** volume_search and catalog_search returned no results for this standardPlace in this run (totalResults/totalHits of 0); collections_search and external_links_search returned substantive hits and are the basis of this guide.

| Repository | Holdings | Access method |
|---|---|---|
| Borthwick Institute for Archives, University of York | Ecclesiastical probate, diocesan and parish records | In-person / written request (http://www.york.ac.uk/borthwick/) |

- Original GRO death certificates are never posted online as images -- only the index is online; the certificate itself must be ordered.

- An 1851 death's probate (if any) predates the 1858 national probate index -- look instead at Yorkshire's ecclesiastical probate records, centered on the Borthwick Institute for Archives.
- Yorkshire genealogical material is frequently split and catalogued by Riding (East/North/West) on Ancestry/Findmypast rather than as a single Yorkshire-wide set -- search all three riding-specific collections, not just a county-wide one.
- Consult GENUKI's Yorkshire page (http://www.genuki.org.uk/big/eng/YKS/) for further parish-level finding aids and local record office contacts.

- **Where held:** FamilySearch digitized collections above; originals at Yorkshire parish churches and diocesan record offices; the Borthwick Institute for Archives, University of York, holds ecclesiastical material (http://www.york.ac.uk/borthwick/, from external_links_search).

- **Testate or intestate:** Both series exist; an 1851 death predates the 1858 national index, so pre-1858 Yorkshire probate (ecclesiastical court records, held at the Borthwick Institute) is the series to search, not the national index.

## Repository guide

### Online repositories
| Repository | Collections for this place | Gap it fills | Access |
|---|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch | England and Wales Death Registration Index 1837-2007 (2285341); England and Wales Census 1851 (2563939); England, Yorkshire, Parish Registers 1538-2016 (4439317); England, Yorkshire, Bishop's Transcripts 1547-1957 (4319956) | Core death index, census corroboration, parish burial cross-check | Free |
| FreeBMD (https://www.freebmd.org.uk/search) | Volunteer-transcribed GRO BMD indexes | Free alternative to subscription BMD index search | Free |
| GRO gov.uk historical index | Births and deaths 1837-1957 | Free index lookup prior to ordering certificate | Free |
| Ancestry | Yorkshire, England, Probate Records 1521-1858; West Yorkshire Church of England Deaths and Burials 1813-1985; North Yorkshire Church of England Deaths and Burials 1813-1995 | Pre-1858 probate; riding-level burial registers | Subscription |
| Findmypast | Yorkshire Burials; Yorkshire Parish Registers and Bishop's Transcripts Browse; England & Wales Deaths 1837-2007 | Burial-specific indexing; browse access to registers | Subscription |

**Coverage of this survey:** volume_search and catalog_search returned no results for this standardPlace in this run (totalResults/totalHits of 0); collections_search and external_links_search returned substantive hits and are the basis of this guide.

### Physical repositories
| Repository | Holdings | Access method |
|---|---|---|
| Borthwick Institute for Archives, University of York | Ecclesiastical probate, diocesan and parish records | In-person / written request (http://www.york.ac.uk/borthwick/) |
| General Register Office (GRO) | Original civil registration certificates (births, marriages, deaths) from 1837 | Order by post/online after finding the index reference |
| Local Yorkshire county record offices (e.g. via Explore York Archives) | Parish chest records, local deposited material | In-person / written request (https://exploreyork.org.uk/archives/) |

## Records NOT online
- Original GRO death certificates are never posted online as images -- only the index is online; the certificate itself must be ordered.
- Pre-1858 Yorkshire ecclesiastical probate records held at the Borthwick Institute are not confirmed as digitized by this run's tool results.

## Known record losses
- No tool result in this run states that Yorkshire's 1851-era civil registration, parish, or probate records were destroyed or lost; none is claimed here.

## Research tips
- Search the quarterly GRO death index first (FreeBMD, Findmypast, Ancestry, or the free GRO gov.uk index) to get the registration district, volume and page before ordering the certificate -- per https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/England_Civil_Registration.
- Cross-check the 1851 census (FamilySearch collection 2563939) for the same person shortly before death, since it can corroborate age, household, and parish of residence.
- Because early civil registration enforcement (1837-1875) was sometimes incomplete, also search the Church of England parish burial register for the township/parish, via the Yorkshire Parish Registers collection (4439317) or Bishop's Transcripts (4319956).
- An 1851 death's probate (if any) predates the 1858 national probate index -- look instead at Yorkshire's ecclesiastical probate records, centered on the Borthwick Institute for Archives.
- Yorkshire genealogical material is frequently split and catalogued by Riding (East/North/West) on Ancestry/Findmypast rather than as a single Yorkshire-wide set -- search all three riding-specific collections, not just a county-wide one.
- Consult GENUKI's Yorkshire page (http://www.genuki.org.uk/big/eng/YKS/) for further parish-level finding aids and local record office contacts.
